item.content:encoded:
The world's two most influential professional science journals probably are Science and Nature. But they no longer limit their jurisdiction to science. Both are now highly ideological to the extent that each has now lent its august pages to boosting the "nature rights" movement.

Science pushed "nature rights" back in 2019. Now Nature has jumped on the bandwagon, publishing an advocacy piece to coincide with Panama's pushing a "Universal Declaration of the Rights of Nature" in the United Nations General Assembly.

The article's title starts out making a hubristic assumption: "Nature has Rights: It's Time the World Recognized Them."

Really? Since when? ...

item.title: Canada Backs Off Euthanasia for Mental Illness, Targets Dementia Patients
item.description: Some are celebrating Canada’s government “indefinitely suspending” legalizing euthanasia for mental illness as a great victory for life. Not me. Let me explain. item.content:encoded:
Some are celebrating Canada’s government “indefinitely suspending” legalizing euthanasia for mental illness as a great victory for life. Not me.

Let me explain. Of course, I am gratified that mental illness will not become grounds for being killed in 2027 as was scheduled. But note: In announcing the suspension, the government mooted legislation likely to pass that would have permanently outlawed killing for mental illness. Moreover, “indefinite” can mean years — or a month. So, it’s not a matter of principle.

But here’s the kicker. The government is now promoting euthanasia for people with dementia. From the Global News story:

[Justice Minister Sean] Fraser also said the government will “grant access to medical assistance in dying to people who have provided consent at a time when they still have capacity but know that they have been diagnosed with an illness that will take that capacity from them subsequently.”

This is sometimes referred to as “advance directive” or “advance request” in medical parlance. It often involves a competent person making a written request for MAID, with the intention that it would be honoured later, if and when they lose the capacity to make the decision for themselves: for example, in people suffering from worsening Alzheimer’s or dementia.

Once this proposal is law, people will be able to order themselves killed in the future when they reach a particular point of incapacity. And they wouldn’t be able to change their minds once they became incompetent because they would no longer be legally entitled to make their own care decisions. So, even if they were happy, not suffering, and now wanting to live, they would still be lethally injected.

This is already the law in the Netherlands and Belgium, and it has led to a horrific story. One Dutch woman signed such a document. When she repeatedly refused the lethal jab after becoming incompetent, the doctor drugged her coffee and started the termination. The patient woke up and struggled against the procedure. The doctor instructed the family to hold her down and completed the killing. Of course, a court later found the doctor not guilty of any crime.

Dementia patients are the next target of the culture of death, with advocacy increasing to include such people in the killable caste. Euthanasia activists already push VSED — suicide by self-starvation — for patients so diagnosed and even want caregivers forced to refuse their patients food and water if the person had so ordered when competent. Once that idea is accepted by society, lethal injections will soon follow because it will be seen as more humane.

So, I am not surprised that Canada’s leaders decided to shift their focus from the mentally ill — which caused a pushback — to cognitively incapacitated patients as euthanasia’s next big expansion. Many are terrified of dementia, so I suspect they believe it will be a lighter lift. And think of the money in health-care resources that will be saved!

item.title: Belgium Expands Killable Caste While Euthanasia Cases Increase

item.content:encoded:
I still marvel at people who think–even after decades of experience with these laws–that legalizing assisted suicide or euthanasia will remain limited to the few for whom nothing else can be done medically to prevent suffering. Not only is it not true, but it is never intended by euthanasia enthusiasts to be so constrained. Indeed, wherever killing as an answer to suffering is legalized, the numbers so dispatched continually rise, the guidelines expand, and euthanasia or suicide as a means of death becomes societally normalized.

In Belgium, that pattern continues. The Belgian Federal Commission for the Control and Evaluation of Euthanasia just issued a press release about its published euthanasia statistics for 2024–2025. A few observations:

  • As I perused the statistics, I was struck by how bloodless and stiflingly bureaucratic this killing machine has become. What was it that the philosopher Hanna Arendt said about the banality of evil?
  • In 2003, there were 259 euthanasia killings. By 2023, there were 3,423, and in 2025, a whopping 4,487, a 31 percent increase from 2023. There will be even more this year, only to be topped every year thereafter going forward. In fact, only during the year of Covid in 2020 did Belgium record fewer euthanasia killings from one year to the next.
  • In 2024–2025, 75.8 percent of the killings were of patients whose deaths were “within the foreseeable future.” That’s not the same thing at all as terminally ill. The rest — 24.2 percent — of the deaths were of people who were not anywhere near a natural death.
  • Two of the killings were for minors under age 18. Expect pediatric euthanasia to increase going forward. Once killing is redefined as a medical “treatment,” how do you deny it to children?
  • Fifteen were by “advance request.” This means incompetent people were killed who could not consent legally to being euthanized at the times of their deaths, and probably could not change their minds about being dispatched either because they were not legally capable of making their own medical decisions.
  • One hundred twenty-nine people with mental illnesses who were not otherwise ill were dispatched. That’s a little less than one every 3 days. Only 9 of these were killed by psychiatrists, meaning doctors who do not specialize in treating mental illnesses killed the rest.
  • Patients (536) were even euthanized in palliative care units. Killing isn’t palliation properly understood, but then, euthanasia corrupts everything it touches.
  • Thousands (2592) of patients were dispatched in hospitals during the two years of the report. Some of these were for the purpose of organ harvesting, but the number of such cases is not discussed.
  • Most of the euthanasia killings (63.5 percent) were carried out by general practitioners. GPs may not know all of the treatment options for serious diseases that require specialized care. A startling 48.4 percent of the killing doctors had no specialized training in end-of-life care.
  • Many more Belgians were probably killed by doctors than the report indicates since terminal sedations are not included in euthanasia statistics.
  • No policy is perfectly carried out, yet zero doctors were reported to courts for abuses. They rarely are anywhere euthanasia and assisted suicide are allowed. And on the few occasions when doctors have been reported, medical associations objected loudly because such cases could have a chilling effect on doctors’ willingness to kill patients.

The same pattern is happening here too, albeit more slowly. But if things keep up the way they are, we will — like our close cultural cousins in Canada — embrace the culture of death with great enthusiasm.
